findings.summary: the stepper was hand-written C++ under a substring gate over the pin's source, which proves the PIN still says something and never that the EMISSION does -- editing the emitted `<=` to `<` left every fragment passing -- and could not see a reordering, because the loop arm and the end arm are both `animation.current = ...`; `advanceSpriteAnimation` and `normalizeDelay` are lowered from their own declarations now and the whole 13-fragment gate is gone

the one capability that blocked AST lowering was four lines: `assignmentTarget` in the pinned numeric lowerer resolved a bound member for reads and not for writes, so a pinned function that mutates the record it was handed could not lower at all -- every future record-mutating pinned body inherits it

three empty `if` blocks left from debugging, one calling `getText()` on every call expression the compiler lowers (7810 on a doom compile) -- and two of them shaped exactly like the entry-source text matching `docs/architecture.md` forbids

the Sprite2D id map is a second copy of the billboard one, and had already drifted from it in three ways the pin does not: a dead handle threw where the pin returns, `clearSprite2DLayer` left the tables naming slots it had dropped, and `0xffffffffu` was written where `invalid_handle` exists

`Number.isFinite` emitted `std::isfinite` in a second place, where `compilePlatformCall` already emits it for the global spelling; both spellings share that arm now, folding where generation settles the argument
`fixedDeltaMs` had no writer -- the option that would set it refuses -- so the record field, its doc, the ternary reading it and the gate fragment covering it were dead in every build

`removeWhenFinished` was a success-shaped `?.cpp === "true"` that silently answered false for anything else, while `loop` two lines above went through `compileCondition`; both settle the same way now, and a value that cannot settle is refused rather than defaulted

`createSpriteAnimationManager` refused on the argument's PRESENCE, so `{}` -- legal upstream and meaning the defaults -- was refused with a message about fields it did not name; it refuses by field through the shared `validateObjectProperties`

the attach refusal claimed "no reached scene does" when both scenes write it, in the arm their own frozen pose folds away -- so a fold regression two files away would surface as this message; it now says what is missing (the hook and its binding) and why the call is unreached

`target.spriteLayerCpp` was concatenated unguarded into the emitted C++, so a handle arriving without its layer would have emitted the literal text `undefined`; the pairing is checked where the kind is
`update_sprite_animation_manager` built a fresh survivor vector every step (43 allocations at the reference pose, measured); `std::erase_if` is one line for eight and allocates none

the three id operations took the id as a `double` and cast it back at every use, though their only callers already hold a `uint32_t`; and `sprite_2d_id_alive` repeated the map lookup instead of calling the slot helper beside it

the runtime record's comment claimed the id tables were "empty until the first addSprite2D", which a default-constructed unordered_map is not -- measured at 2 allocations and 152 bytes on this toolchain; the comment says what is actually true instead
the TODO's "Integrate first" header said 44 over a list of 43, having been decremented rather than recounted -- and was already off by one before this branch; it is recounted

the `parseFloat` carry was asked to route through `materializeBrowserPrimitive` for reuse, and does NOT: that helper renders its cpp with `compileNumber(expression)`, which for this expression re-enters the arm it was reached from. Measured by trying it -- the suite failed with a stack overflow on the existing 'does not browser-fold ordinary parseFloat calls' test. The value is returned already settled, with the reason recorded where the choice is made
